Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
716 PM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

.SYNOPSIS...20/1019 PM.

Dry and cooler weather is expected through Sunday morning. AThere
will be a chance of light rain Sunday and Sunday night. Light 
rain is possible again Tuesday night into Wednesday. Thanksgiving 
will be dry and warmer.

&&

.SHORT TERM (SAT-TUE)...21/130 PM.

For the short term period, latest models indicate no major changes
to previous forecast thinking. Main concern will be rain chances
on Sunday then again on Tuesday.

With respect to rain, the first weak system will impact the area 
on Sunday and Sunday night. Rain will develop across the Central
Coast Sunday morning then work its way south and east Sunday
afternoon and night. Based on current guidance, measurable
rainfall is likely for most areas with the chances across the
Antelope Valley noticeably lower. Totals will not be overly
impressive with this system and latest QPF guidance has backed off
on the area totals. At this time, totals look to be one quarter
inch or less with the "highest" totals across San Luis Obispo
county. 

The second system will begin to impact northern areas late in the
day on Tuesday (and continuing through Wednesday which will be 
discussed in the extended discussion). Through Tuesday evening,
this second system will bring 0.10 inches or less to San Luis
Obispo county (with the highest totals around Rocky Butte). 

In between these two systems, an upper level ridge will keep the
area dry on Monday and through most of Tuesday. A warming trend
can be expected for most areas through Tuesday. There will a a
couple degrees of warming Sunday and Monday. However, some weak
offshore flow on Tuesday will allow for more pronounced warming
west of the mountains with high temperatures topping out in the
upper 60s to mid 70s.

.LONG TERM (WED-SAT)...21/130 PM.

For the extended, latest models continue to be on the same broad
synoptic page, resulting in no significant changes to previous
forecast thinking. 

On Wednesday, a weak system will move across the area. At this
time, the GFS and its ensembles are a bit slower and wetter with
this system than the ECMWF contingent. With this system, San Luis
Obispo and Santa Barbara counties look to have the highest rain
chances and totals. For these counties, rainfall totals between
0.10 and 0.25 inches look good with higher amounts, up to 0.75
inches, across the northwest corner of San Luis Obispo county. For
Ventura and LA counties, the rain chances will be much lower (20%
or less) and any measurable rainfall will only be on the order of
a few hundredths of an inch.

For Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, the combination of an upper
level ridge building overhead and weak offshore pressure gradients
will bring warm and dry conditions to the area. High temperatures
west of the mountains will climb into the 70s (about 4-8 degrees
above normal) and into the 60s across interior sections (2-4
degrees above normal). With the offshore pressure gradients, there
will be some offshore winds, especially on Friday morning. At this
time, the chances for any advisory-level winds remain quite low
(under 10%). 

On Saturday, the upper ridge breaks down and another system will
impact the area. At this time, this particular system looks to be
weak, just like its predecessors. Some light showers (likely 
under 0.10 inches) will be possible with a few degrees of cooling.

&&

.AVIATION...22/0316Z.

At 00Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Good confidence in TAFs. VFR TAFs expected at all airfields thru 
Sun morning, although there is a 20% chance for cigs at KPRB from
11Z to 16Z. 

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Light northeast winds are
possible from 09 to 16Z. Any east wind component is expected to 
be 7 kt or less thru the fcst period.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...21/123 PM.

Good confidence that winds and seas will remain below small craft
advisory (SCA) levels through Tuesday.

Two storms one later Sunday and overnight and another Wednesday.
These systems will bring the best chance of rain to the seas north
of Pt Conception. Post-frontal low-end SCA level NW-W winds will 
still be possible Wednesday/night south of Point Conception. A 
significant westerly swell (around 14-16 feet) is expected mid- 
week, with large, SCA level seas for the outer waters.

&&

.BEACHES...21/120 PM.

There is significant concern for moderate to major coastal 
flooding Thanksgiving week. This is due to the combination of 
kelvin wave/thermal expansion, Pergiean spring tides, and a large 
long-period westerly swell (260-280 degrees).

===============================================================

[For Central Coast, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY is in effect for Monday- Tuesday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated damage 
to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is unlikely. 

A COASTAL FLOOD WATCH is in effect for WEDNESDAY- THURSDAY.

The swell will arrive during this period which will combine with 
the aforementioned factors. Still some uncertainty in regards to 
how timely these will combine, but regardless significant impacts 
seem probable. Timing of peak high tides are expected between 845 
AM-1000 AM and predicted values are: roughly 8.2-8.4 ft for 
LA/VTA and 7.9-8.2 ft for Central Coast. The reasonable worst case
scenario is 0.3-0.5 ft above these values. A slight limiting 
factor that may prevent the worst case scenario from materializes 
would be higher mean sea level pressure.

Potential impacts if upgraded to COASTAL FLOOD WARNING:

More extensive moderate coastal flooding reaching further inland,
moderate to high risk of damaging flooding of coastal roads and 
structures, and significant beach erosion is likely.

Areas of greatest concern: Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes, 
& Cayucos/Avila/Pismo Piers. For LA: Santa Monica to Palo Verdes 
and Long Beach/Naples. For VTA, Faria to Silver Strand Beach 
including inside of harbors and Ventura Harbor.

A HIGH SURF ADVISORY has been issued for the Central Coast from 
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon.

Surf of up to 11 feet expected Monday morning with a lull in high
surf Monday night into Tuesday followed by rapid building to 
10-15 feet Wednesday morning and to 15 to 20 feet Wednesday 
afternoon and evening with the potential for even higher surf. 
There is an increasing likelihood the High Surf Advisory will 
need to eventually be upgraded to a High Surf Warning probably by 
Tuesday.

For the Ventura and Los Angeles County beaches, elevated to high 
surf is expected for much of the upcoming week, peaking Wednesday 
and Thursday with likely High Surf Advisories. There is even the 
small chance of Warning-level surf up to 15 feet for the Ventura 
County coast during this period.

==================================================================

[For Santa Barbara South Coast & Catalina/Santa Barbara islands]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY has been issued for Monday-Thursday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated
damage to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is
unlikely. 

Areas of greatest concern: Santa Barbara to Rincon and Jalama
Beach. 

Additional Information: Elevated to high surf is likely through
Thanksgiving week. Additional coastal hazards will likely be
needed for Friday.

==================================================================

In conclusion, this is a particularly concerning period for 
coastal flooding risks and high surf - Please read the "actions" 
section below. 

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS:

(1)Heed advice from local officials - Rely on their expertise
regarding preparedness, closures, and warnings. 

(2)Protect property - Take necessary actions such as setting up
sandbags or barriers in flood-prone areas.

(3)Avoid flood areas - Stay clear of rock jetties, and flooded
roads, walkways, and other normally dry places.

(4)Stay off the beach - large breaking waves can cause injury, 
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near 
shore.

(4)Monitor the forecast for latest information: weather.gov/LOX
and @nwslosangeles on social media. Be aware of when high tide
peaks in your area: tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov. Refer to LAXCFWLOX.
